claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with: **Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you asking about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child. I'm asking about my son Alex, who's 16 and still in school.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'd like to ask a few more questions about your situation to determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Now I need to ask:

**Does Alex live with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Since Alex is 16 and you mentioned he's still in school, I need to clarify:

**Is Alex in approved education or training? This would typically include things like:**
- A-levels or Scottish Highers
- T-levels
- NVQs up to level 3
- Home education (if it started before they turned 16)
- Other non-advanced education (up to level 3)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. I just have a couple more questions:

**Is Alex working 24 hours or more per week, or is he claiming any benefits in his own right (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not working that much - he's focused on his studies. And he doesn't claim any benefits himself.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect, thank you. One final question:

**Are you responsible for Alex - meaning you live with him (which you've confirmed) and/or you pay towards his upkeep (such as food, clothes, pocket money)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, of course - I'm his parent and I look after him. I pay for everything he needs - food, clothes, all his expenses.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:

✓ You live in the UK  
✓ Alex is 16 and in approved education (A-levels at sixth form college)  
✓ Alex lives with you  
✓ You are responsible for him and pay for his upkeep  
✓ Alex is not working 24+ hours per week  
✓ Alex is not claiming benefits in his own right  

Since Alex is 16 and continuing in approved education, you can continue to receive Child Benefit for him until he turns 20, as long as he remains in approved education or training.

**Important reminder:** If you or your partner have an individual income over £60,000, you may need to pay the High Income Child Benefit tax charge. You can use the government's Child Benefit tax calculator to work out if this applies to you.

If you haven't already claimed Child Benefit, you can apply through the government's website or by contacting HMRC.
